title: Text wraps to a width, and a box can size itself to its text
body:
A label breaks lines only at a `\n` in its string, so the step paragraphs in `key-schemes.acre` hold hand-placed line breaks. A `box` takes a fixed `size`, so the boxes of its section 1 are sized by trial.

## Proposal

- `width N` on `text` and on a box's text wraps lines at spaces to fit N pixels, using the measure from the shaping issue. A `\n` still forces a break.
- A `box` without `size`, or with `size auto`, takes the size of its text plus `padding`, a new property.
- Text inside a box can align `left`, `center` or `right`, with a padding, instead of always being centered.

## Open

- Whether a box's text should place by its first baseline or its top. Top matches `text` today.
close_reason: Landed uncommitted on dev: text::layout wraps at spaces within a width (text::wrap), width on text and on a box's text, and padding, text-align and an optional size on box. figures/key-schemes.acre uses them for section 1's boxes and section 4's steps.
